title: Scaling Perspectives — Program Editor
description: Built an internal programme editor that let clinical teams create new therapeutic programmes without engineering involvement, cutting creation time by 75% and enabling parallel development across conditions.

metrics.label: reduction in time to create a programme.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: VP of Product at Koa Health, post-clinical-success phase of Perspectives. Team: product, clinical, and engineering.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: The bottleneck to expanding the Perspectives programme library was content creation. Each new programme required clinical design, product specification, engineering build, QA, and clinical validation — a full development cycle per condition. At that rate, expanding from 4 conditions to 10+ would take years. The business problem was time-to-market: competitors were moving and clinical partners were waiting.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I personally owned the product definition, the design of the editor, and the stakeholder alignment across clinical, product, and technical teams. I managed the engineering delivery. Clinical workflow research with MGH and Harvard was led by me directly; the technical implementation was delegated to engineering.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: The core architectural decision was to separate content creation from platform delivery — building a CMS layer that gave clinical and content teams control over programme structure, module sequencing, content, branching logic, and personalisation rules without code changes. I ran research with MGH and Harvard clinical teams to understand how they actually worked and translated that into tool requirements. The hardest design decision was calibrating how much flexibility to give clinical teams: too rigid and the tool couldn't handle the breadth of conditions needed; too open and there was regulatory and therapeutic integrity risk. I designed a constrained editor with a structured review and sign-off workflow to balance both.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• Programme creation time reduced by 75%
  • Parallel development across multiple conditions became possible for the first time
  • Clinical teams took creative ownership of programme content, reducing back-and-forth with engineering on every iteration
